predecessors.name: Eastern Roman Empire
predecessors.text: infobox 'Preceded by: Byzantine Empire; Kingdom of the Lombards': the Samnite lands of the southern Apennines on the Lombard-Byzantine frontier

successors.name: Papal States
successors.text: 'little but the city remaining' when Guiscard returned the title to the papacy in 1081

successors.name: Norman Italy
successors.text: the principality's countryside and counties, held by Norman counts (the Norman page names Boiano, granted to Rudolf of Moulins, and Ariano), by the 1081 'little more than Benevento and its environs'

ledger.x: 577: the Lombard duchy of Benevento under Zotto, 'Duke of Benevento'.
741: Cliopatria's shape has grown from 35.9k to 46.3k km2, eastwards and southwards.
758: King Desiderius invades.
759: the duchies rise again.

774: after Charlemagne's conquest of the Lombard kingdom 'Arechis II took the title of princeps (prince)' instead of the royal dignity, and the duchy becomes the Principality of Benevento; infobox 'Established: 774', 'Sovereign state (774-787)'.
778: Cliopatria's shape loses about 3,700 km2 around Chieti.
840: Siconulf, freed by Amalfitan merchants after Radelchis seized Benevento on Sicard's murder in 839, is 'proclaimed prince in Salerno' and holds the west.
840-851: the decade-long civil war between Radelchis at Benevento and Siconulf at Salerno.
851: 'Louis, King of Italy, divided the principality into two sections'.
880: Cliopatria's shape drops about 10,000 km2 east of lon 15.4.
899: 'In 899, Atenulf I of Capua conquered Benevento and united the two duchies.'
967: Otto I gives Pandulf Ironhead Spoleto and Camerino.
978: Salerno passes to Pandulf Ironhead.
March 981: Pandulf Ironhead dies and his lands are partitioned.
981: 'Otto II came down to Rome in 981, however, and Spoleto was given to Thrasimund IV,' duke of Camerino.
990: Cliopatria draws Capua apart again (384 km2) and Benevento shrinks to 12,882 km2.
1010-1014: Capua's land is in the Benevento shape again (13,218 km2) and Cliopatria's Capua row is absent.
1015: Capua returns as a separate shape.
1022: Henry II's expedition.
1022: the emperor withdraws after the failed siege of Troia; no separate date for the withdrawal.
1034: Cliopatria's shape loses about 455 km2 on its western edge, where Cliopatria's Capua shape of 1034 reaches (lon 13.40).
1040: 'The Prince of Salerno Guaimar IV took control of Benevento in 1040.'
1040: the western edge moves from lon 13.87 to 13.95, where Cliopatria's Norman Italy shape of 1040 (1,249 km2, from lon 13.40) lies.
1047: Henry III confirmed Aversa and Drogo as his vassal, 'Guaimar was demoted to prince of Salerno, and Capua went to Pandulf IV'.
1053: Benevento passes under the pope.
1078: 'Pope Gregory VII appointed Guiscard Prince of Benevento in 1078'.
1081: 'Finally, in 1081, Guiscard returned the title to the papacy with little but the city remaining.'
1081: the Principality of Benevento ends; no prince is named afterwards.

wars.name: Constans II's expedition against Benevento
wars.outcome: Constans II landed at Taranto and besieged Benevento in 663; Duke Romuald I defended the city and destroyed part of the Roman army at Forino.

wars.name: Desiderius's capture of Benevento
wars.outcome: Desiderius 'briefly captured' Spoleto and Benevento in 758; both duchies rebelled in 759 while he was in the Roman Campagna.

wars.name: Frankish and Byzantine attacks on the principality
wars.outcome: 787: Charlemagne's siege of Salerno forced Arechis II to submit to Frankish suzerainty.

wars.name: Beneventan civil war
wars.outcome: Radelchis (Benevento) and Siconulf (Salerno) fought for about ten years; Lothair I's mediators proposed a division in 847; Louis divided the principality in 851.

wars.name: Byzantine reconquest of Apulia
wars.outcome: Bari passed to the Byzantines in 876, Otranto was taken in 873, and Nikephoros Phokas the Elder's expeditions of the mid-880s extended Byzantine control over most of Apulia and Calabria; the theme of Longobardia dates from c.

wars.name: Pandulf Ironhead's war with the Byzantines
wars.outcome: Pandulf was captured at the Battle of Bovino in 969 and jailed in Constantinople; in 970 the Byzantines besieged Capua in his absence.

wars.name: Henry II's expedition of 1022
wars.outcome: Henry II conquered both Capua and Benevento but withdrew after the failed siege of Troia.

wars.name: Norman conquest of southern Italy
wars.outcome: The Normans defeated the catepan at Montepeloso on 3 September 1041, captured Leo IX at Civitate on 18 June 1053 and held him in Benevento; the principality came under papal suzerainty in 1053, Robert Guiscard was its prince 1078-1081 and gave it back to the…

certainty.note: No page opened gives a boundary line for the duchy or principality; the division of 851 and the partition of 981 are dated but their lines are only described by the cities listed.
